sections.title: v0.26.2
items: v0.26.1 can no longer join: import the new pack, or let the Modrinth App update your instance.
Chat works: messages are no longer refused with "chat is not allowed".
Smoother by default: on first launch the pack turns VSync off, sets the framerate to unlimited and the brightness to Bright. Change them afterwards and your settings stay.
Our own names in the menus: the gun controls and settings now read "Great War Gun Settings".

sections.title: v0.26.1
items: v0.26 can no longer join: import the new pack, or let the Modrinth App update your instance.
The menus are quiet for now: the old background sound is gone until the event's own track is ready. The intro's booms still play.
The map's far-out views come with the pack again, from the updated map, so they load instantly.
Tidier mod details in the game's mod list.

sections.title: v0.26
items: The build for the tester event. v0.25 can no longer join: import the new pack, or let the Modrinth App update your instance.
Soldiers move and heal differently: new stamina, running speed and bandage behaviour, with new settings for them.
Staff can set up battles for testers: two sides, tickets, a round timer, capture points, class kits when you come back, tanks for each side, and the winner announced at the end.

sections.title: v0.25
items: The pack for the tester event. v0.24 can no longer join: import the new pack, or let the Modrinth App update your instance.
While a contested zone is open, soldiers of every nation at war can cross the land around it to get in.
Regions border each other only where the map says they do, not wherever two regions happen to touch.
Constantinople's and Petrograd's capitals moved into their cities.
Safer spawns: spawn areas are always on fairly level ground under open sky, never on a cave floor.
No more freeze when a crowd of soldiers comes back at the same time.
The map is fairer: a region's name on the map no longer hints at anything hidden, and the map can't be asked for more than the server allows.
Mountains, the Arctic and the desert no longer claim to be impassable.

sections.title: v0.24
items: v0.23 can no longer join: import the new pack, or let the Modrinth App update your instance.

Region borders follow real 1914 lines: provinces, governorates and départements where the history is known, rivers and ridges elsewhere. Every region keeps its name, owner and capital, and Kotor now belongs to Dalmatia, as it did in 1914.
A region's core is now a field command post, the same for every nation.
Leaders choose where their region's core stands from a few good spots, and can move it; moving costs money and takes time, and a new site starts half fortified.
Holding a core means standing at it: soldiers swimming, in a boat, flying or dug in underneath don't count.
Neutral land is slower to claim: anyone else there stands against the claim, and it takes three times as long.
Nobody comes back into a siege: spawn areas and homes are kept well away from every core.
The world has an edge: a border stops you at the edge of the map, and beyond it there is nothing.
The map's borders are drawn from historical sources; their credits are on the map screen.

sections.title: v0.23.1
items: A server-only fix, no new pack: keep using v0.23.

Fixed a rare problem where part of the map could be replaced by random new terrain when it was saved and loaded at almost the same moment. The whole map was checked afterwards and nothing was damaged.

sections.title: v0.23
items: The war map is new: press K to open it (J stays with the machine-gun mount). It shows the real terrain of the whole front.
Zoom smoothly from all of Europe down to single regions, with borders drawn at every zoom.
Search the map for a region or a capital, and hover over a region to see its owner and capital.
The far-out map views come with the pack; close-up views load as you look at them and are kept on your computer, so the second time is instant.
What your map shows depends on who you are: scouts and their leadership see what a scouting run revealed, while it lasts.
The world isn't drawn behind the map while it's open, so the map runs smoothly; the game carries on around you.
Uniform wear after a revive now counts from the revive, not from your first day in the war.
Smoother server: saving the map's regions and placing region cores no longer stalls the server.
Older packs (v0.22.1 and before) can no longer join, and your key bindings reset to the pack's defaults once.

sections.title: v0.22.1
items: New blocks from the old pale forests: pale oak logs, wood, planks and leaves, pale moss, hanging moss and eyeblossoms, for the new world map.
Dressing stations, dugouts, observation posts, shrines, village houses and supply dumps can now hold what soldiers left behind.
Loot never includes ammunition or medical kits: those still come from the Armory.
A server restart during the Christmas Truce no longer announces the truce twice, and everyone is still sent home when it ends.
The "In combat" timer no longer shows after you die.

sections.title: v0.22
items: Your first day of daily orders now reads "a streak has begun" instead of "1 days in a row".
War windows now follow a fixed schedule of evenings, known in advance, so nobody loses land while asleep.
Front-line weather: each war window has its own forecast, rain or light mist, printed in the paper the day before.
Tanks lose some grip in the rain.
The Christmas Truce on 25 December: no fighting, football in no man's land, parcels across the wire and carols.
Truce parcels leave the other soldier a keepsake with both your names on it.
After-action reports in the paper when a war window closes, naming the best soldiers and the costliest fight.
A nation that has lost ground two windows running rallies: its soldiers' daily orders count double toward promotion.
Daily orders: three small jobs a day from what your nation needs, with a bonus for days in a row.
Regiments of 3 to 10 soldiers with a name, a tag and a banner.
Mentors: experienced soldiers can take a new recruit under their wing and earn a ribbon when the recruit is promoted.
Medals and ribbons you can see, on your uniform and your service record.
Your rank shows on your sleeve, and officers wear their own cap and belt.
Ottoman soldiers have their own full set of uniforms for every class.
Your uniform gets dirtier the longer you survive, and is clean again after a death.
Medics are paid for healing wounds the enemy dealt.
The death recap: when you fall, a card shows who got you, with what, from how far, and how your life went.
Your issued kit is yours: it can't be dropped, sold or handed over.
Killing a soldier who carries only the free kit pays nothing.
Spawn protection now ends the moment you fire a weapon or hit a tank.
A fair start for late joiners, who no longer begin far behind everyone else.
The Field Service Pocket Book: a new soldier's first hour in eight illustrated pages, always in your pocket.
Winter greatcoats for every army, plus a knitted balaclava and gloves, as cosmetics.
Army rations and a field kitchen: cooked rations leave you well fed and refill your stamina.
Dog tags drop from the fallen, and memorials keep their names.
Field post: write cards and letters to your comrades, delivered as postcards when they next log in.
Trench art: carve spent tank shell cases into brass keepsakes that carry your name.
New dugout furniture, from a wire bed to a dartboard and a looted armchair.
Builders' commissions: buildings your nation commissions and you build, with your name on a brass plaque.
The fallen who can't return can write for the paper as war correspondents and call the front in the wager.
Since you were away: after an hour or more offline, a few lines at login tell you what changed.
Ores no longer grow in ordinary ground: resources come from the mines.
Large furniture and double doors now place as one block.
New field signs at nodes, showing the holder's flag.
Tank interiors cleaned up, with new fittings inside.
No more advancement pop-ups for every gun, and no movement tutorial on your first join.
Joining with nothing on now gives you your nation's uniform.
Pay rebalanced so nations' treasuries no longer run dry on the first day.
Many fixes from the testers and our own checks: kill pay, combat logging, protected property, crossings, the shop and more.

sections.title: v0.21
items: Ranks and gear: you start as a Private with a cap, a uniform and your nation's rifle, and rank up to unlock better gear.
Armour, guns and melee weapons are made at your nation's Armory from materials and money.
Five armour tiers, with star upgrades on each piece.
Stamina: running with a gun tires you, and heavier guns and armour tire you faster.
Machine guns on mounts: set one up on the ground, man it and feed it belts; explosives can destroy a mount.
Every gun now has hip fire, recoil and aim sway.
Eight national grenades: hold to prime and cook them, release to throw.
New materials: steel from the steel furnace, plus copper, salt, cotton, saltpetre, rubber and elite plate.
The recipe book shows where every material comes from.
Uniforms and armour get dirtier, scratched and torn as they wear down.
Thousands of new blocks for trenches, bunkers, dugouts, towns, hospitals and mines.
Doors, gates, shutters and trapdoors that open.
Blocks now blend into the blocks beside them, so ground and walls no longer show hard edges.
Barbed wire, stakes and other defences now hurt those who cross them.
No names showing through walls.
The tester session runs as short rounds, with a bar at the top of your screen showing the round, the score and the time left.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 21
items: Dying is now a short wait: the death screen shows for a few seconds, then you watch a living teammate until you respawn.
Click to switch which teammate you watch; with nobody to watch you see a timer.
You respawn at your capital after about 2 minutes, or about 5 during a war window.
If your capital is held by the enemy, nobody respawns until it is retaken.
After 24 hours without its capital, a Leader can move the capital to another node the nation holds.
A nation now lives as long as it holds at least one node.
A nation that can't pay its upkeep loses its least valuable nodes first, never its last.
War windows: nodes can only be captured during scheduled windows.
Borders between enemies are shut between windows, and anyone left in enemy land is sent home when a window ends.
Contested zones close during war windows.
Nations now mark each other as ally, neutral or enemy from one screen in the Cabinet.
Justice is simpler: a killing leads to forgiveness, compensation, a fine or expulsion instead of long trials.
Income and upkeep now depend on how valuable each node is.
Research can unlock extra respawn points, and you come back at the nearest one to where you fell.
The Arctic and the desert hurt you and can't be built on.
Tanks can't enter mountains or marshes, and neutral countries are closed.
Scouts can't attack while across a shut border, and must stay inside a node for a while to gather intel.
Beta 21.2: each tank crew seat can only look along its own arc again; the tank camera stays free.
Beta 21.2: with the visor shut, the driver's view narrows to the slit.
Beta 21.3: fixed your controls not working after a respawn until you rejoined.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 20
items: Behind-the-scenes tidying only; nothing changes in game.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 19
items: The server now checks your mods and resource packs when you join: only the official pack gets in.
If something doesn't match, the message tells you exactly what to remove or reinstall.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 18
items: New Fast mode in Settings for big battles or weaker computers.
Fast mode shortens view distance, cuts particles and clouds, and skips cosmetics, ragdolls and long deaths.
Turning Fast mode off puts your old settings back.
The servers were tested with 300 test bots and tuned so busy fights don't drop everyone.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 17
items: VIP and VIP+ now come from your Discord roles.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 16
items: VIP+ kills now end in a ragdoll: the body falls loose and is thrown by whatever killed it.
Only a few bodies stay at once; the oldest sinks away first.
Reduced effects keeps the old ending.
Your death screen now waits until your death camera has finished.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 15
items: Server-side work only; nothing changes in game.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 14
items: Regions now yield what the map says: coal, iron, gold, diamond, oil or farmland.
Your nation is paid for its land every hour again.
Farmland grows crops faster and harvests more, up to each region's limit.
Oil derricks with a working pump fill barrels in oil land.
Tanks need fuel again: refuel them with oil barrels or fuel cans.
Mines are built into the map: their ore comes back over time, up to an allowance each session.
Only the region's own nation, or an enemy at war, can mine there.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 13
items: The front is now one server per nation plus one for neutral lands, all at the same address.
Crossing into another nation's land shows a short "Crossing into..." card and brings your kit, wounds, money and tank along.
During war preparation the border between the two sides closes, except to Scouts.
Wars are fought on their own war servers, and captured land stays with whoever took it.
Chat, the tab list, news and notices work across every server.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 12
items: VIP and VIP+ cosmetics, open them with /cosmetics, from War Office Settings or from the title screen.
Uniform trims, shield crests, personal items like a pipe, scarf, whistle or medals, and kill effects.
Each tank can wear a paint scheme, a unit emblem and your own or an ally's flag.
VIP+ adds cinematic deaths for the players you kill, a death effect and a kill message.
[VIP] and [VIP+] badges in chat, the tab list and name tags.
New settings: blood on or off, hide other players' cosmetics, and reduced effects.
Everything is cosmetic: nothing sold changes how you fight.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 11
items: Everyone now has 40 health, twice the hearts.
Natural healing is slow, so bandages matter more, and Medics heal more.
Guns now hit by type, not by model; a rifleman at full health always survives one body shot.
A gun takes a moment to raise after sprinting or switching.
Machine guns only fire when you are lying down or braced on sandbags, and they are heavy.
Armour is one simple table, and the most it can ever stop is 30 %.
Armour pieces wear out after a number of hits, and can be upgraded at a crafting table or an anvil.
New body armour: padded vest, steel body shield and heavy trench armour, worn over your uniform.
Iron, chainmail and diamond armour are gone, and villagers no longer sell them.
New melee weapons: trench knife, bayonet, cavalry sabre, entrenching tool and trench club.
New trench shield that blocks a set number of blows and can be mended at an anvil.
Vanilla swords and shields are gone, and axes hit like pickaxes.
New /recipes book shows everything you can craft or buy, its price and the research it needs.
Tanks hurt people twice as much to match the bigger health bar.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 10
items: Before an update restart you get a minute of warnings and a countdown on screen.
The HUD tells you when a session is about to begin, has just begun or is ending.
The War Office now lists the rule that logging out in a fight counts as death.
The Armory can sell several of one item in a single purchase.
Backups now run every hour and before every update.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 9
items: The shops follow the session: counters can be closed, and the Armory sells only up to the session's tier.
Crops grow slower in hot and cold lands, and melons, pumpkins and bamboo grow faster in the jungle.
Hot or cold water hurts you after a few seconds.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 8
items: Logging out during a fight now counts as dying; a timer under your money shows when you are in combat.
Staff show a badge and are listed first.
Fewer mobs: hostile mobs are capped and none spawn in caves.
Creepers and zombie villagers don't spawn at all.
Fewer animals spawn, and each player can breed a limited number per session.
Enchantments are capped at sensible levels.
TNT can no longer be crafted.
Fixed rifle bullets passing through the Fiat 2000 and the A7V in some spots.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 7
items: The war now runs in sessions, shown in the War Office with a calendar.
Some sessions can be ceasefires with fighting switched off.
New players start on safe ground inside their nation's spawn area.
Contested zones: protected areas that open and close with the session, where nobody can build or break.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 6
items: You can no longer raise a shield with a gun in hand, and bullets pass straight through raised shields.
Helmets that look like steel helmets now protect like steel helmets.
The server handles big battles better, with faster saving.
Region resources, oil and tank fuel arrived briefly, then were taken out again in beta 6.1 until the map was ready.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 5
items: The bell-like chime on tank reloads is gone; reloads now sound like a heavy breech.
The pay coin sound no longer plays while you are in a tank.
Tanks now have the real shape of their models: stand on the roof, fall through gaps, no more getting stuck on corners.
Where you hit a tank matters: the front is toughest, the rear and engine weakest.
Armour was rebalanced: uniforms show your side, helmets and body armour stop part of the damage.
An unused add-on was removed, so the pack is smaller and starts faster.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 4
items: The intro plays once each time you start the game, and leaving a server takes you straight back to the menu.
Only the war's own items exist in the game; everything else is hidden and can't be crafted or kept.
The game you install is a client-only build and can't host a singleplayer world.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 3
items: The inside of a tank no longer jumps against the walls while the hull turns.
The flat sheets in front of the Mark V gunners' eyes are gone.
The "xylophone" sound of moving tanks is gone: tracks clank and the turret cranks.
Engines and tracks can be heard much further away, and a cannon's boom carries far.
Inside a tank, outside sound is muffled.
Rifles and machine guns are now inaccurate unless you aim, and you can't fire while sprinting.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 2
items: Guns hold, aim, reload and fire properly again, and the purple shot is gone.
Modern guns stay out of the war and are taken away if anyone has one.

sections.title: v0.20 beta 1
items: Tanks arrive: the British Mark V, the German A7V, the Italian Fiat 2000 and the French Renault FT.
Each crew seat has its own view, with the driver, gunners and a loader who speeds up reloads.
Right-click to board, Shift to get out, Left Alt to change seat, R to reload, and the comma key for hints.
Hold right click for the gun sight, and press F5 for the tank camera.
Guns turn only within their own arcs, and shells fly with real drop.
Tanks need ammunition: restock at the Motor Pool or with a tank ammunition crate.
Big firing effects: smoke, dust, shaking ground, layered sound, and hits that look different on earth, stone, wood, water and armour.
Tank shells never break blocks.
Nations build tanks at their Motor Pool, with limits on how many each can have.
Repair kits mend tanks, and Assault soldiers can stick a Bundle Charge on an enemy tank.
Two new nations join the war: the Ottoman Empire and Bulgaria, making eight.
Some nations build tanks under licence from their allies at a higher cost.
Name tags now update straight away when someone changes nation.

sections.title: v0.19
items: Keybinds sorted out: the event's controls no longer fight each other, and your own changes are kept.
The War Office opens on P and the Cabinet on I.
The game window is now called The Great War and has its own icon.
If you are disconnected after playing, you see Minecraft's usual screen again.
Minecraft's own menus and screens stay as you know them.

sections.title: v0.18
items: A new title screen with a Join the war button that takes you straight to the front.
The title screen shows whether the front is online and a public record of your soldier.
If joining fails, a clear message tells you why.
A new opening intro with a dark bunker atmosphere, which you can skip or watch again.
A moving background behind the main menu.
Choose a class; your first choice is free and comes with an issued kit.
Some classes are limited in number per nation.
Medics heal much better with bandages.
Pick a specialisation: Miner, Farmer or Builder.
Earn pay for time served and for fighting, and rise through the ranks.
Your rank is shown before your name.
Win medals that make the newspaper.
Your record keeps your kills, captures, defences, earnings and days survived.
Land now produces resources and money for the nation that holds it.
Ore only comes from ore veins in mining regions, and veins grow back.
Farms are limited by the land a nation holds.
Sell resources to your nation at the Supply Office in your capital.
Buy weapons, ammunition and your nation's uniforms at the Armory.
Nations can order production of weapons and gear.
Each class can only fire its own guns; pistols work for everyone.
Armour now stops bullets depending on the piece and your class.
A steel helmet can save you from one deadly headshot.
A healthy soldier in a tunic can't be killed by a single body shot.
Weapons can only come from the Armory; other sources are blocked.
Run your own stall from a chest to sell items to other players.
Your buildings and chests are protected from other nations, at peace and at war.
Lock your own chests and containers.
Sandbags and barbed wire can be crafted and placed; the wire slows and hurts anyone caught in it.
Gas masks are now for sale.
Nations can post Fortify jobs that pay you for building defences in their land.
Coal can now be traded between nations.
Land upkeep for nations is now switched on.
Our screens hide chat and the HUD while open.

sections.title: Early development, phase 17
items: A new look for every screen, with sounds and motion you can turn down in Settings.
The Leader's screen is now called the Cabinet.
Button results now show inside the screen.
The pause screen is back to normal.

sections.title: Early development, phase 16
items: One Leader runs each nation, helped by eight seats with their own powers.
The War Office: your own page with your standing, orders, the newspaper, the wanted list and the map.
The four rules of the war are shown when you first join.
Nations send each other mail: alliances, peace, calls to arms, trade and demands for justice.
Nations can trade money and resources.
The Daily Front newspaper reports the war, with one article per nation per day.
Rallies and paid jobs from your nation.
Leave your nation, or ask to join another.

sections.title: Early development, phase 15
items: All deadlines now run on plain real time.
War requests now need a reason.

sections.title: Early development, phases 13 to 14
items: Incidents, charges, settlements, exile and full trials with verdicts.
Link your account to the companion website.

sections.title: Early development, phases 11 to 12
items: Nations have leadership with powers and a line of succession.
Wars now start from a request, then a preparation period, then open war.
Allies can never hurt each other.

sections.title: Early development, phases 9 to 10
items: Killing your own countrymen is treason and leads to fines or outlaw status.
Outlaws lose their nation and can be hunted.
Post bounties on outlaws and enemies; the killer claims them.
A justice screen with the wanted list and trial boards.
Nations must pay upkeep for their land or lose it, and can go bankrupt.
Players deep in debt feel it.

sections.title: Early development, phases 5 to 7
items: Everyone has a money balance, shown in the corner and above name tags.
Nations have a treasury and set their own income tax.
A shared research tree that members fund by donating resources.

sections.title: Early development, phases 3 to 4
items: The land is divided into natural regions, each with an unbreakable core.
Capture a region by holding its core with more living soldiers than the defenders.
Capitals are harder to take, and losing one ends the nation.
Rival nations block each other when claiming neutral land.
A full-screen war map drawn from the real terrain.
Scouts can spy on enemy regions for a while.

sections.title: Early development, phases 1 to 2
items: You join one of the fixed nations, balanced so no side is crowded.
Death is permanent: the dead become spectators.
Your nation tag shows in chat and the player list.
You can only hurt players of nations you are at war with.
Wars end only when both sides agree to peace.
